claims.text: The studied material is a dual-nanoprecipitation Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy produced by additive manufacturing.
In-situ (S)TEM with EDS/EELS can track oxidation-induced morphological and elemental changes in this alloy.
Three-dimensional atom-probe tomography can resolve local post-oxidation elemental distributions in the oxide scale and interfacial regions.
High-temperature oxidation causes local diffusional rearrangement of Al, Cr, and Ti within or from the nanoprecipitates.
The oxidation-induced redistribution of Al, Cr, and Ti produces stable oxide layers.
The resulting stable oxide layers improve the alloy's high-temperature oxidation resistance.
An oxidation temperature range of 800–1000 °C is representative of typical gas-turbine operating conditions.
The alloy contains nanoscale precipitates formed by Al and Ti.
The Al- and Ti-containing nanoscale precipitates provide a protective oxidation barrier.
Al, Cr, and Ti dynamically redistribute toward the oxidized surface.
Redistributed Al, Cr, and Ti form stable, adherent oxide scales.
Stable, adherent oxide scales reduce oxidation kinetics.
Real-time precipitate morphology and elemental diffusion pathways correlate with increased oxide protection and improved oxidation resistance.
Post-exposure characterization without in-situ tracking provides limited information about dynamic oxidation phenomena.
Above 1000 °C or at longer exposure times, additional phase transformations may occur.
Above 1000 °C or at longer exposure times, oxide spallation may occur.
Correlating local composition variations with local oxidation rates may be non-trivial.
Electron-microscopy artifacts may complicate interpretation of the measurements.
Sputtering or related atom-probe artifacts may complicate interpretation of local elemental distributions.

contradictions.description: The intervention states that atom-probe tomography is performed while the alloy is exposed to the oxidative environment, whereas the experiment specifies that the pillars are retrieved after oxidation and then analyzed by APT.
